F. Prepare to Install the Airstair
SUBTASK 52-61-10-860-024
(1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open and have safety tags:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4
Row Col Number Name
A 16 C00409 FWD AIRSTAIR DOOR
A 17 C00246 FWD AIRSTAIR CONT NORMAL
A 18 C00270 FWD AIRSTAIR TREAD LIGHT
B 17 C00850 FWD AIRSTAIR ACTUATOR
C 16 C01254 FWD AIRSTAIR CONT STBY
C 17 C00411 FWD AIRSTAIR STBY DOOR ACTR
SUBTASK 52-61-10-980-012
(2) Make sure the swing arm will be clear of the airstair as follows:
(a) Temporarily hold the swing arm clear of the airstair.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-220-005
(3) Make sure that the distance between the forward and aft rails is to 35.64 ±0.01 in.
(905.26 ±0.26 mm).
NOTE: Measure from the top inner flanges of each rail.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-980-013
(4) Make sure the electrical connectors on the rails will be clear of the airstair as follows:
(a) Temporarily hold the electrical connectors clear of the airstair.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-820-005
(5) Align the ladders to the carriage.
(a) Disconnect the coupling [5] on the actuator drive shaft [6].
(b) Move the ladders to align the index slot [7] in the carriage to the index hole in the ladder.
1) If the ladders will not move, manually turn the actuator drive shaft [6].
NOTE: You can use a rag or belt wound tightly around the shaft to turn manually.
(c) Put the no. 1 rig pin, STD-1323 through the index slot [7] in the carriage and the hole in
the ladder truck [8].
(d) Connect the coupling [5] on the actuator drive shaft [6].
(e) Remove the no. 1 rig pin, STD-1323.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-860-025
(6) Make sure the carriage step is down.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-860-026
(7) Put the pinion disconnect lever in the not locked position.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
G. Installation
SUBTASK 52-61-10-480-004
CAUTION
DO NOT USE THE HANDRAILS TO LIFT THE AIRSTAIR. USE THE CORRECT
TOOL TO LIFT THE AIRSTAIR. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE AIRSTAIR
OR THE AIRPLANE IF YOU DO NOT USE THE CORRECT TOOL.
(1) Do one of these steps to lift the airstair:
(a) Use the sling, SPL-1978 and the 500 lb capacity hoist, STD-1098. Put the airstair
equipment, SPL-14636 on the hydraulic jack, SPL-1561 with its telescoping hydraulic
adapter assembly, SPL-1584.
NOTE: For installation instructions, refer to the tool placard.
1) If necessary, use the sling, SPL-1978 and the 500 lb capacity hoist, STD-1098 to
install the airstair onto the airstair equipment, SPL-14636.
2) Safety the airstair as shown on the tool placard.
3) Disconnect the sling, SPL-1978 from the 500 lb capacity hoist, STD-1098.
4) Remove the sling, SPL-1978 from the airstair.
(b) Attach the sling, SPL-1978 to the airstair.
1) Connect the sling, SPL-1978 to the 500 lb capacity hoist, STD-1098.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-980-014
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE LOWER LADDER STAYS IN ITS POSITION WHILE
YOU MOVE THE AIRSTAIR. THE LOWER LADDER WILL OPERATE OUT-OF￾SEQUENCE IF IT MOVES. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT IF
YOU OPERATE THE AIRSTAIR.
(2) Use the 500 lb capacity hoist, STD-1098 or the hydraulic jack, SPL-1561 to lift the airstair.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-980-015
CAUTION
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU MOVE THE AIRSTAIR. MAKE SURE THAT YOU
HOLD THE AIRSTAIR CORRECTLY. IT IS EASY TO CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
AIRSTAIR AND THE STRUCTURE.
(3) Carefully move the airstair adjacent to the airstair door opening.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-980-016
(4) Align the airstair with the rails.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-980-017
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE CARRIAGE PINIONS ENGAGE THE FORWARD AND
AFT RAILS AT THE SAME TIME. THE AIRSTAIR WILL NOT MOVE FREELY IF
THE PINIONS DO NOT ENGAGE THE RAILS AT THE SAME TIME.
(5) Move the airstair until the carriage fully engages the rails.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-080-002
(6) Lower the 500 lb capacity hoist, STD-1098 or the hydraulic jack, SPL-1561 until it does not
hold the airstair.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 52-61-10-080-003
(7) If necessary, disconnect the 500 lb capacity hoist, STD-1098 from the sling, SPL-1978.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-080-004
(8) If necessary, remove the sling, SPL-1978 from the airstair.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-980-018
(9) Move the airstair until it is against the inboard stops.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-860-027
(10) Move the pinion disconnect lever to the locked position.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-420-002
(11) Do these steps to install the step actuator blocks on the outboard end of the forward and aft
rails:
(a) Put the shims and step actuator blocks in place.
(b) Install the step actuator blocks to the rails.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-420-003
(12) Install the outboard carriage extend stops on the outboard end of the two rails (Figure 401).
(a) Put the shims in between the outboard carriage extend stops and the rail.
(b) Temporarily attach the outboard carriage extend stops to the rails.
(c) Move the pinion disconnect lever to the not locked position.
(d) Move the carriage outboard until it touches the outboard carriage extend stops.
(e) Measure the clearance from the carriage to the roller on one of the outboard carriage
extend stops as follows:
1) Make the carriage touch the roller on one of the outboard stops.
2) Make sure the clearance at the roller on the other outboard stop is from 0.005 in.
(0.127 mm) to 0.040 in. (1.016 mm).
3) If necessary, change the thickness of the shims below the outboard stops to get the
correct clearance.
NOTE: The shims below the two outboard stops must be the same thickness.
(f) Move the carriage until it touches the inboard stops.
(g) Attach the outboard stops to the rails permanently.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-980-019
(13) Pull the airstair outboard until the airstair actuator [4] is above the access door in the electronic
compartment.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-420-004
(14) Install the swing arm as follows (Figure 402):
CAUTION
DO NOT INSTALL THE SWING ARM WITH THE ENDS DOWN. IF THE
ENDS POINT DOWN, THE SWING ARM AND THE WIRE CAN BREAK.
THIS CAN CAUSE SPARKS, FIRE AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(a) Attach the swing arm to the bracket on the airstair actuator [4].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE CONDUIT SWING ARM BETWEEN THE
AIRSTAIR CARRIAGE AND THE LADDER IS IN ITS CORRECT POSITION.
IF IT IS INCORRECTLY ALIGNED , IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(b) Make sure both ends of the swing arm point up.
(c) Connect the airstair P6 connector.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-220-003
(15) Do a check of the support bracket adjustment as follows:
(a) Measure the dimensions shown in (Figure 402).
(b) Change the thickness of the shims if it is necessary to get the dimensions shown.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-220-004
(16) Do a check of the airstair movement as follows:
NOTE: Manually move the airstair inboard and outboard to examine the airstair.
(a) Make sure the clearance between the airstair and the door opening is more than 0.25 in.
(6.35 mm).
(b) Make sure the step on the carriage moves up.
(c) Make sure the airstair does not hit the structure.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-410-001
(17) Install the S3/S4 SWITCH RAMP located on the airstair carriage.

SUBTASK 52-61-10-080-005

SUBTASK 52-61-10-080-006
(2) Adjust the S3 and S4 switches. Do only the steps in "Prepare for the S3 and S4 Switch

(1) Align the carriage to the rails and lock the pinion disconnect lever as follows:

(b) Put the no. 2 rig pin, STD-1324 through the carriage retract index hole and aft rail index
slot.
(c) Move the pinion disconnect lever to the locked position.
(d) Use MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048 to lock the pinion disconnect lever.
(e) Remove the no. 2 rig pin, STD-1324.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-020-012
(2) Connect the airstair P1 electrical connector.

 ALL

SUBTASK 52-61-10-860-015
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THERE ARE NO PERSONS OR EQUIPMENT IN THE
AREA OF THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR BEFORE IT OPERATES. THE AIRSTAIR
CAN HIT PERSONS OR EQUIPMENT WHEN YOU OPERATE IT. IF THE
AIRSTAIR HITS PERSONS OR EQUIPMENT, INJURY TO PERSONS OR
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(WARNING PRECEDES)
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR IN LESS THAN 20 MINUTES
AFTER 3 FULL CYCLES THAT ARE ONE AFTER THE OTHER. DO NOT
OPERATE THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR WHEN THE WIND IS MORE THAN 40
KNOTS. DO NOT OPERATE THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR WHEN THE
FORWARD ENTRY DOOR IS BETWEEN THE COCKED AND FULLY OPEN
POSITIONS. DO NOT OPERATE THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR WHEN THERE IS
NO SUPPORT BELOW THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR (AS AN EXAMPLE, WHEN
THE AIRPLANE IS ON JACKS). IF YOU OPERATE THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR
WITH ONE OR MORE OF THESE CONDITIONS, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT
CAN OCCUR.

52-61-10-211-801Top Step Actuator CheckPDF p. 1262
3. Top Step Actuator Check
A. References
Reference Title
52-61-00-860-801 Forward Airstair Extension (P/B 201)
52-61-00-860-802 Forward Airstair Retraction (P/B 201)
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 52-61-10-860-033
(1) Prepare for the Check:
(a) Forward Airstair Extension, TASK 52-61-00-860-801
(b) Get access to the top step actuation rollers and actuator blocks.
SUBTASK 52-61-10-211-001
(2) Examine the top step actuation rollers and actuator blocks:
(a) If a roller or an actuator block shows signs of damage or excessive wear, then replace it.
(b) Make sure that a minimum of 50% of the two rollers engage with the two actuator blocks.
1) If a minimum of 50% of the rollers engage with the actuator blocks, then the check
is complete.
a) Forward Airstair Retraction, TASK 52-61-00-860-802
2) If the rollers are not correctly engaged in the actuator blocks, then continue.
(c) Make a record of the estimated distance needed so that the two rollers will correctly
engage the actuator blocks.
(d) Forward Airstair Retraction, TASK 52-61-00-860-802
(e) Measure the distance between the forward and aft airstair rails:
1) The distance between the top inner flange of the two rails must be 35.62 ±0.06 in.
(90.47 ±0.16 cm).
a) If the distance between the rails is not in the limits, then adjust the rail on the
side where the roller is not correctly engaged.
b) If the distance between the rails is in the limits, then continue.
(f) Remove the actuator block from the side where the roller is not correctly engaged.
(g) Get access to aluminum that has a thickness to match your estimated distance above.
(h) Make a shim that is the shape of the actuator block.
(i) Install the actuator block with the shim.
(j) Forward Airstair Extension, TASK 52-61-00-860-801
(k) Make sure that a minimum of 50% of the two rollers engage with the two actuator blocks.
(l) Forward Airstair Retraction, TASK 52-61-00-860-802

G. Extend Limit Switches (S3 and S4) Adjustment
SUBTASK 52-61-15-820-002
(1) Adjust the S3 switch:
(a) To adjust the S3 extend limit switch for the normal system, connect the digital/analog
multimeter, COM-1793, between terminal Y1 on the K1 relay and pin 5 on the airstair P1
electrical connector.
(b) Make sure that the multimeter indicates continuity.
1) If the multimeter indicates no continuity, turn the adjustment nuts for the S3 switch
until the indication is continuity.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Turn the adjustment nuts until digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, indicates no
continuity.
(d) Tighten adjustment nuts.
(e) Make sure that the no. 2 rig pin, STD-1324, is not installed.
(f) Slowly move the airstair carriage inboard, then outboard.
(g) Use the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, to make sure that the S3 switch operates
when the extend index slot and carriage extend index slot align.
1) Use the no. 2 rig pin, STD-1324, to make sure that the slots align.
(h) Make sure that the S3 switch operates when the switch roller is in the correct position on
the switch ramp (Figure 401).
(i) Make sure that the no. 2 rig pin, STD-1324, is not installed.
(j) Put MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, on the retract S3 switch adjustment nuts.
(k) Disconnect the multimeter.
SUBTASK 52-61-15-820-004
(2) Adjust the S4 switch:
(a) To adjust the S4 extend limit switch is for the standby system, connect the digital/analog
multimeter, COM-1793, between terminal Y1 on the K2 relay and pin 17 on the airstair P1
electrical connector .
(b) Make sure that the multimeter indicates continuity.
1) If the multimeter does not indicate continuity, turn the adjustment nuts for the S4
switch until the indication is continuity.
(c) Turn the adjustment nuts until digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, indicates no
continuity.
(d) Tighten the adjustment nuts.
(e) Make sure that the no. 2 rig pin, STD-1324, is not installed.
(f) Slowly move the airstair carriage inboard, then outboard.
(g) Use the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, to make sure that the S4 switch operates
when the extend index slot and carriage extend slot align.
1) Use the no. 2 rig pin, STD-1324, to make sure that the slots align.
(h) Make sure that the S4 switch operates when the switch roller is in the correct position on
the switch ramp (Figure 401).
(i) Make sure that the no. 2 rig pin, STD-1324, is not installed.
(j) Put MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, on the retract S4 switch adjustment nuts.
(k) Disconnect the multimeter.

DO NOT OPERATE THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR WHEN THE WIND IS
MORE THAN 40 KNOTS. DO NOT OPERATE THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR
WHEN THE FORWARD ENTRY DOOR IS BETWEEN THE COCKED AND

(c) Pull the wires up through the stanchion.
NOTE: The string extends out of the stanchion to show the location of the wires.
(d) Disconnect the string from the wires.

between the center of the bolt holes in the rod ends.

G. Adjustment of the Forward Airstair Ladder Speed-up Operating Switch (S13)
SUBTASK 52-61-21-820-003
(1) Adjust the S13 switch:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Make sure the switch actuator roller touches the flat part of the ramp.
(b) Turn the locknuts until the switch plunger lightly touches the actuator.
(c) Connect the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793 across the switch:
1) Disconnect the airstair P20 electrical connector.
2) Attach one test lead to pin 10 of the P1 connector.
3) Attach the other test lead to terminal 4 of airstair terminal block TB2.
(d) Make sure there is no continuity across the switch.
(e) Turn the locknuts until the plunger goes into the switch to the dimension shown in
(Figure 401).
(f) Make sure that there is continuity across the switch when the ramp pushes the plunger.
(g) Tighten the locknuts.
(h) Disconnect the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793.
(i) Connect the airstair P20 electrical connector.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE CONDUIT SWING ARM BETWEEN THE
AIRSTAIR CARRIAGE AND THE LADDER IS IN ITS CORRECT POSITION.
IF IT IS INCORRECTLY ALIGNED , IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(j) Make sure that the swing arm conduit is correctly aligned.
SUBTASK 52-61-21-020-009
(2) Connect the airstair P1 electrical connector.

CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE GEARBOXES IN THEIR
CORRECT POSITIONS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE
EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(a) Make sure the gearbox turns in the correct direction.
1) A clockwise input to a forward gearbox gives a counterclockwise output.
2) A clockwise input to an aft gearbox gives a clockwise output.

assembly.

4. Forward Airstair Ballscrew Endplay Adjustment
(Figure 202, Figure 203)
A. References
Reference Title

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left
C. Prepare for the Adjustment
SUBTASK 52-61-23-010-001
(1) Remove the outboard bearing block [41]:
(a) Remove the nuts [32] and bolts [33] that attach the outboard bearing block [41] to the
carriage.
(b) Remove the nut [46] and the washer [45] from the end of the ballscrew [1].
(c) Remove the outboard bearing block [41] from the ballscrew [1].
D. Adjustment
SUBTASK 52-61-23-820-008
(1) Adjust the ballscrew [1] endplay:
(a) Change the thickness of the shims [42], [48] on the ballscrew [1] to adjust the endplay:
1) Remove laminations from the shims [42], [48] to decrease the play in the end of the
ballscrew [1].
SUBTASK 52-61-23-420-016
(2) Install the outboard bearing block [41] on the ballscrew [1]:
(a) Put the shims [42], [48] and the spacer [44] on the end of the ballscrew [1].
(b) Put the key [42] on the ballscrew [41].
(c) Turn the bearing in the outboard bearing block [41] until the key [42] aligns with the slot in
the bearing.
(d) Push the outboard bearing block [41] until the bearing touches the spacer [44].
(e) Put the washer [45] on the ballscrew [1].
(f) Put the nut [46] on the ballscrew [1].
(g) Tighten the nut [46] from 70 to 100 pound-inches (7.9-11.3 newton-meters).
(h) Install the bolts [33] and nuts [32] to attach the outboard bearing block [41] to the
carriage.
SUBTASK 52-61-23-720-001
(3) Do this task: Forward Airstair Ballscrew Assembly End Play Check, TASK 52-61-10-200-801.
SUBTASK 52-61-23-820-009
(4) If the endplay is not correct, adjust it.
SUBTASK 52-61-23-840-001
(5) If the endplay is correct, bend the tang of the washer until it touches the nut.

(b) Turn the ballscrew [1] until the ballnut [2] aligns with the ballnut [2] on the other
ballscrew [1] as shown in (Figure 203).
(c) Engage the shaft coupling [29] with the splines on the ballscrew [1].
(d) Put the pin [28] through the shaft coupling [29].
(e) Install a cotter pin [30].

WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THERE ARE NO PERSONS OR EQUIPMENT IN THE
AREA OF THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR BEFORE IT OPERATES. THE AIRSTAIR
CAN HIT PERSONS OR EQUIPMENT WHEN YOU OPERATE IT. IF THE
AIRSTAIR HITS PERSONS OR EQUIPMENT, INJURY TO PERSONS OR
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
CAUTION
DO NOT OPERATE THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR IN LESS THAN 20 MINUTES
AFTER 3 FULL CYCLES THAT ARE ONE AFTER THE OTHER. DO NOT
OPERATE THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR WHEN THE WIND IS MORE THAN 40
KNOTS. DO NOT OPERATE THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR WHEN THE
FORWARD ENTRY DOOR IS BETWEEN THE COCKED AND FULLY OPEN
POSITIONS. DO NOT OPERATE THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR WHEN THERE IS
NO SUPPORT BELOW THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR (AS AN EXAMPLE, WHEN
THE AIRPLANE IS ON JACKS). IF YOU OPERATE THE FORWARD AIRSTAIR
WITH ONE OR MORE OF THESE CONDITIONS, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT
CAN OCCUR.

F. Forward Airstair Ladder Tread Assembly Removal
SUBTASK 52-61-25-020-001
(1) To remove one of the lower ladder tread assembly [1], do these tasks:
(a) Disconnect the plug connector [2] (P19), if necessary.
(b) Remove the screws [3], washers [4], and clamps [5], if necessary.
(c) Remove the tie wraps [14], if installed, that attach the cables to the tread assembly [1].
(d) Remove the screws [6], screws [7], washers [8], washers [9], and nuts [10] that attach the
tread assembly [1].
(e) Lift off and remove the tread assembly [1].
(f) Do this procedure again for the removal of the other lower ladder tread assembly [1].
SUBTASK 52-61-25-200-001
(2) Examine the bonded tread [13] for damage, cracks and worn areas.
(3) If the bonded tread [13] replacement is necessary, replace the bonded tread [13].
SUBTASK 52-61-25-020-004
(4) To remove the bonded tread [13], do these tasks:
(a) Apply 200°F (93°C) to 250°F (121°C) heat to the tread to make the material soft and
prevent it from cracks.
(b) Remove the tread slowly.
(c) Clean the remaining adhesive on the tread assembly surface with a solvent, B00148 .
SUBTASK 52-61-25-400-002
(5) To install a new bonded tread [13], do these tasks:
(a) Apply one layer of sealant, A50193 with a brush to the tread assembly.
(b) Let it set for 5 to 8 minutes until tacky.
(c) Remove the paper from the new tread with adhesive.
(d) Apply 200°F (93°C) to 250°F (121°C) heat to the tread to make the material soft and
prevent it from cracks.
(e) Put the tread around the edge of the step and gradually lower the tread to the tread
assembly.
(f) Push the tread with a heavy roller to remove air bubbles.
(g) Apply the adhesive, A00441 to seal all the edges of the tread.
(h) Clean unwanted adhesive with a solvent, B00148.
SUBTASK 52-61-25-020-002
(6) To remove one of the upper ladder tread assembly [15], do these tasks:
(a) Disconnect the plug connector [16] (P14), if necessary.
(b) Remove the screws [17], washers [18], nuts [19] and clamps [20], if necessary.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Remove the screw [21], washer [22], nut [23] and clamp [24], if necessary.
(d) Remove the screw [25], washer [26] and clamp [27], if necessary.
(e) Remove the tie wraps [14], if installed, that attach the cables to the tread assembly [15].
(f) Remove the screws [28], screws [29], screws [30], washers [31], washers [32] and
nuts [33] that attach the tread assembly [15].
(g) Lift off and remove the tread assembly [15].
(h) Do this procedure again for the removal of the other upper ladder tread assembly [15].
SUBTASK 52-61-25-200-002
(7) Examine the bonded tread [36] for damage, cracks and worn areas.
(8) If the bonded tread [36] replacement is necessary, replace the bonded tread [36].
SUBTASK 52-61-25-020-003
(9) To remove the bonded tread [36], do these tasks:

prevent it from cracks.
(b) Remove the tread slowly.
(c) Clean the remaining adhesive on the tread assembly surface with a solvent, B00148 .
SUBTASK 52-61-25-400-001
(10) To install a new bonded tread [36], do these tasks:

52-61-50-400-803Forward Airstair Door AdjustmentPDF p. 1375
5. Forward Airstair Door Adjustment
(Figure 403)
A. General
(1) The door is adjustable for flushness and edge gap clearance. These adjustments are
somewhat inter-related. Changing one adjustment may affect other adjustments.
(2) This task makes adjustments on the door to get these three conditions:
(a) The outer door skin must be in permitted flushness tolerances with relation to the outer
fuselage skin.
(b) The relation of the door and carriage mechanism must be correct for the door to move
smoothly to and from the open position.
(c) The horizontal and vertical adjustments of the door in the door opening have these two
conditions:
1) The eight stop pins on the door touch near the center of the stop pads on the door
opening.
2) The clearance between the door skin outer edge and the fuselage outer skin is in
the permitted tolerances.
NOTE: The horizontal adjustment is in a forward or aft direction in the door
opening. The vertical adjustment is in a vertical direction in a relation to the
plane of the door opening.

52-61-53-000-802 Forward Airstair Door Lockpin and Lockpin Actuator Removal

E. Prepare for the Adjustment
SUBTASK 52-61-50-420-008
(1) Prepare the door for the adjustment:
(a) Make sure lock springs are removed from the stop pins and guide pins.
(b) Make sure the door stop pins and guide pins are fully retracted.
(c) Turn the guide pins away from the center of the door two full turns.
(d) Loosen the eight bolts that attach the lower guide fitting to the door until the lower guide
fitting is free to move horizontally and vertically.
SUBTASK 52-61-50-420-009
(2) Prepare the airplane for the door adjustment:
(a) Make sure the airplane is not on jacks.
(b) Make sure the door is open and the airstair is retracted.
(c) Make sure the standby door actuator motor is not installed. If necessary, do this task:
Forward Airstair Door Actuator Standby System Motor Removal,
TASK 52-61-59-000-801.
(d) Make sure the bolts that attach the center guide fitting to structure are loose.
(e) Make sure the lockpin is retracted. If it is necessary, retract the lockpin:
1) Do this task: Forward Airstair Door Lockpin and Lockpin Actuator Removal,
TASK 52-61-53-000-802.
NOTE: Do only the steps to remove one extension rod from the rocker arm.
2) Secure the lockpin actuator to structure to prevent accidental motion and damage.
SUBTASK 52-61-50-860-020
(3) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4
Row Col Number Name
A 16 C00409 FWD AIRSTAIR DOOR
A 17 C00246 FWD AIRSTAIR CONT NORMAL
A 18 C00270 FWD AIRSTAIR TREAD LIGHT
B 17 C00850 FWD AIRSTAIR ACTUATOR
C 16 C01254 FWD AIRSTAIR CONT STBY
C 17 C00411 FWD AIRSTAIR STBY DOOR ACTR
F. Initial Adjustment
SUBTASK 52-61-50-420-010
(1) Turn the actuator manual drive to move the door to the closed position.
SUBTASK 52-61-50-420-011
(2) Do the initial adjustment of the door:
(a) Move the door so that the stop pins are near the center of the stop pads (Figure 402).
(b) Turn the forward and aft lower stop pins outboard until they touch the stop pads.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Move the lower guide fitting on the door, until the stop pins touch near the center of the
stop pads.
CAUTION
DO NOT REMOVE MATERIAL FROM THE DOOR OPENING. IF
MATERIAL IS REMOVED FROM THE DOOR OPENING THE DOOR WILL
NOT FIT.
(d) If it is necessary, trim the door edge.
(e) Apply corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 to the areas of the door that do not have
corrosion protection (SRM 51-20-01).
(f) If it is necessary, install the door.
G. Adjustment
SUBTASK 52-61-50-210-007
(1) Adjust the flushness of the door upper edge (Figure 404):
(a) Loosen the screws that attach the upper ends of the door tracks to structure.
(b) Move the door tracks inboard or outboard to get the flushness dimension shown in
(Figure 403)
(c) Tighten the screws that attach the upper end of the door tracks to structure.
SUBTASK 52-61-50-210-008
(2) Adjust the flushness of the door lower edge (Figure 404):
(a) Turn the lower forward and aft stop pins inboard or outboard to get the flushness shown
in (Figure 403).
NOTE: If necessary, turn the actuator manual drive to allow the door to move inboard or
outboard.
(b) Turn the lower forward and aft stop pins inboard until the nearest stop pin and bushing
groves align.
(c) Install lock springs on the lower forward and aft stop pins.
NOTE: The flushness adjustment of the lower edge of the door can affect the door
lockpin clearance.
SUBTASK 52-61-50-210-009
(3) Adjust the stop pins to the center of the stop pads (Figure 402):
(a) Move the door horizontally and vertically to get the stop pins correctly positioned on the
stop pad centers (Figure 402).
SUBTASK 52-61-50-210-010
(4) Adjust the vertical clearance of the door (Figure 401):
(a) Add and remove shims under the two vertical alignment rollers to get the door top and
bottom clearance dimensions shown in (Figure 403).
NOTE: The final thickness of the forward shim pack may differ from the final thickness of
the aft shim pack.
SUBTASK 52-61-50-210-011
(5) Adjust the horizontal clearance of the door (Figure 401):
(a) Move the door horizontally to get the correct forward and aft gap clearance as shown in
(Figure 403).
(b) Tighten the bolts that attach the center guide fitting to structure.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 52-61-50-210-012
(6) Align the door in the door track (Figure 405):
(a) Make sure the door is in the closed position.
(b) Turn the guide pins to get the clearance shown in (Figure 405).
(c) Install the locksprings in the guide pins.
(d) Move adjustment washers between the door track side of the guide arm and door side of
the guide arm to get the guide roller to engage the door track to the dimension shown in
(Figure 405).
(e) Make sure at least one guide roller washer is on each side of the guide arm.
(f) Install a new MS27111-2 locking key washer.
NOTE: Key washer may be reused if alternate unused key-tabs are available and
previously used key-tabs are removed. Discard key washers with cracks.
(g) Tighten the nut that attaches the guide roller to the guide arm.
(h) Bend the tabs of the MS27111-2 locking key washer as shown in (Figure 405)to safety it.
(i) Make sure two keys of the MS27111-2 locking key washer are flat against the edges of
the nut.
(j) Manually move the door to the fully open position.
(k) Manually move the door to the fully closed position.
(l) Make sure the there is no binding or interference between the guide pins and door tracks.
(m) Turn the guide pins in the direction of the center of the door until the nearest lockpin
grooves in the guide pin and guide pin bushing align.
(n) Install lock springs in the guide pins.
SUBTASK 52-61-50-210-013
(7) Adjust the stop pins without locksprings as follows (Figure 402):
NOTE: The lower forward and aft stop pins are the only ones that should have locksprings
installed.
(a) Make sure the lower forward and aft stop pins touch the stop pads.
(b) Turn the stop pins outboard until they touch the stop pads.
(c) Turn the stop pins inboard until the nearest lock spring grooves in the stop pin and
bushing align.
(d) Install the locksprings in the stop pins.
(e) Make sure that the stop pins touch the stop pads in the location shown in (Figure 402).
SUBTASK 52-61-50-210-014
(8) Make sure the door flushness and clearance are within permitted specifications (Figure 403).
SUBTASK 52-61-50-210-015
(9) Tighten the bolts that attach the lower guide fitting to the door.
SUBTASK 52-61-50-210-016
(10) Connect the lockpin:
(a) Do this task: Forward Airstair Door Actuator Standby System Motor Installation,
TASK 52-61-59-400-801.
NOTE: Do only the steps to connect the extension rod to the rocker arm.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Do this task: Forward Airstair Door Lock Mechanism Adjustment and Test,
TASK 52-61-53-820-801.
SUBTASK 52-61-50-210-017
(11) If the door closed limit switches require adjustment, do this task: Forward Airstair Door Closed
Switch Adjustment and Test, TASK 52-61-60-820-801.
NOTE: Do only the steps to adjust the door closed limit switches.
SUBTASK 52-61-50-210-018
(12) If the door open limit switches require adjustment, do this task: Forward Airstair Door Open
Limit Switches (S201 and S205) Adjustment, TASK 52-61-61-820-801.
NOTE: Do only the steps to adjust the door open limit switches.

52-61-50-210-801Forward Airstair Door Seal InspectionPDF p. 1389
2. Forward Airstair Door Seal Inspection
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. References
Reference Title
52-61-00-710-802 Airstair Door Operation Without Airstairs Installed (P/B 201)
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left
C. Inspection
SUBTASK 52-61-50-210-001
(1) Do a visual inspection of the door pressure seal as follows:
(a) Open the airstair door but do not extend the airstair, if necessary, do this task: Airstair
Door Operation Without Airstairs Installed, TASK 52-61-00-710-802.
(b) Examine the seal.
1) Look for cracks, holes, and tears.
2) Look for indications of seal deterioration.
3) Make sure the seal is correctly installed in the seal retainer.
(c) Close the airstair door, if necessary, do this task: Airstair Door Operation Without Airstairs
Installed, TASK 52-61-00-710-802.

bottom guide fitting.

diameter holes align, adjust the bottom guide fitting.
NOTE: You can adjust the bottom guide fitting vertically and horizontally by the serrations on
the base. You can add or remove shims to adjust in the inboard and outboard
direction.

 ALL

SUBTASK 52-61-52-020-001

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Remove the screws [22], [25], locknuts [20], washers [21], support brackets [23], and
bonding jumper [14] that attach the aft switch bracket [1] and forward switch bracket [5] to

that attach the actuator [4] to the actuator support [9].

clearance between the lockpin [1] and the crossbolt [6] is as shown (Figure 501).

G. Forward Airstair Door Lock Mechanism Adjustment
SUBTASK 52-61-53-820-001
(1) Adjust the lockpin [1] extended position:
(a) If they are installed, remove the castelated nuts [7], cotter pins [8], washers [9], and
bolts [10] that attach the normal system extension rod [2] and the standby system
extension rod [4] to the rocker arm [5].
(b) Turn the normal system extension rod [2] and the standby system extension rod [4] until
you get these conditions:
1) The vertical clearance between the top of the lockpin [1] and the crossbolt [6] is as
shown (Figure 501).
NOTE: You must temporarily install the bolts through the extension rods and rocker
arm to measure the vertical clearance.
2) The dimension between the bottom of the normal system extension rod [2] and the
standby system extension rod [4] and the top of the actuators [3] is as shown
(Figure 501).
(c) Loosely install the washers [9], bolts [10], and castelated nuts [7] that connect the normal
system extension rod [2] and the standby system extension rod [4] to the rocker arm [5].
(d) Make sure that the horizontal clearance between the lockpin [1] and the crossbolt [6] is
as shown (Figure 501).
(e) Make sure the lockpin [1] height above the sill web is 0.085 in. (2.16 mm) - 1.150 in.
(29.21 mm).
NOTE: This is an approximate dimension and can change if the forward airstair door
height changes.

(3) Adjust the lockpin [1] retracted position:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Move the crossbolt [6] above the lockpin [1]:
1) Open the access door to get to the exterior control switches.
2) Move the exterior control to the NORMAL EXTEND position until the clearance
between the outboard bottom edge of the airstair door and the outboard bottom
edge of the door opening is 0.550 in. (13.97 mm) - 0.750 in. (19.05 mm).
3) Look through the door opening to make sure the crossbolt [6] is above the
lockpin [1].
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS NO POWER TO THE DOOR ACTUATOR
MOTORS. THE DOOR ACTUATOR MOTORS CAN OPERATE IF THE
POWER IS ON. IF THE DOOR ACTUATOR MOTORS OPERATE, INJURY
TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(b) Remove power from the door actuator motors:
1) Disconnect the D912 and D914 electrical connectors from the door actuator motors.
(c) Make sure the retracted lockpin [1] is in the correct position:
NOTE: Two persons are necessary to do this task.
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY POWER TO THE ACTUATORS FOR MORE THAN
120 SECONDS. WHEN YOU APPLY POWER TO THE ACTUATORS
FOR MORE THAN 120 SECONDS, DAMAGE TO THE ACTUATORS
CAN OCCUR.
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY POWER TO THE ACTUATORS FOR MORE THAN 5
CYCLES, ONE AFTER THE OTHER ONE. SPECIFY A CYCLE BY A
TIME OF POWER APPLIED TO THE ACTUATOR FOLLOWED BY AN
EQUAL QUANTITY OF TIME WITH THE POWER OFF. IF POWER IS
APPLIED TO THE ACTUATORS FOR MORE THAN 5 CYCLES, ONE
AFTER THE OTHER ONE, DAMAGE TO THE ACTUATORS CAN
OCCUR.
1) Move the exterior controls to the NORMAL EXTEND position to retract the
lockpin [1].
a) While the lockpin [1] is retracted, make sure the vertical clearance between
the lockpin [1] and crossbolt [6] is as shown (Figure 501).
b) Release the exterior control.
2) If it is necessary, turn the normal system extension rod [2] to get the correct
clearance between the lockpin [1] and the crossbolt [6].
3) Move the exterior controls to the STANDBY EXTEND position to retract the
lockpin [1].
a) While the lockpin [1] is retracted, make sure the vertical clearance between
the lockpin [1] and crossbolt [6] is as shown (Figure 501).
b) Release the exterior control.
4) If it is necessary, turn the standby system extension rod [4] to get the correct
clearance between the lockpin [1] and the crossbolt [6].
5) When the lockpin [1] is retracted with NORMAL power, make sure the clearance
between the lockpin [1] and crossbolt [6] is correct.
6) Connect the D912 and D914 electrical connectors to the door actuator motors.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
7) Use the exterior controls to open and close the forward airstair door.
8) Make sure the clearance between the top of the lockpin [1] and the crossbolt [6] is
as shown (Figure 501).
(d) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, between the washers [11] and jamnuts [12] on the
actuators [3].
(e) Install the cotter pins [8] in the castelated nuts [7] that connect the normal system
extension rod [2] an the standby system extension rod [4] to the rocker arm [5].
SUBTASK 52-61-53-410-003
(4) Close this access panel:
Number Name/Location
117A Electronic Equipment Access Door
SUBTASK 52-61-53-820-004
(5) Do this task: Forward Airstair Door Lockpin Sensor S282 Adjustment, TASK 52-71-61-820-801.
SUBTASK 52-61-53-710-003
(6) Do a test of the forward airstair lockpin mechanism:
(a) Put the airstair controls in the NORMAL EXTEND position.
1) Make sure the airstair door opens.
2) Release the controls when the airstair door is fully open.
(b) Put the airstair controls in the NORMAL RETRACT position until the airstair door is fully
closed.
(c) Put the airstair controls in the STANDBY EXTEND position.
1) Make sure the airstair door opens.
2) Release the controls when the airstair door is fully open.

Number Name/Location

closed) as follows:
1) Measure the thickness of the clay, G02020 at the center of the mark in the clay.

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Move the switch inboard by the amount of clearance measured from the mark in the
clay, G02020 plus 0.07 to 0.11 inch (1.78-2.79 mm).

STANDBY mode to operate the door.
2) Make sure the switch operates correctly to stop the actuator.
3) Make sure the STAIRS IN OPERATION light at the internal control panel goes off
when the door is closed.
4) Make sure the AIRSTAIR light at the Forward Overhead Panel, P5, is off when the
door is closed.
(b) Do a check of the forward airstair door:

117BL Forward Airstair Door

117BL Forward Airstair Door
electrically.

bearing plates.
(c) If the airstair door does not fully close, do the steps as follows:

forward airstair door to fully close.

 ALL

ATA 52-61-62

2 tasks
52-61-62-020-801Forward and Aft Rail RemovalPDF p. 1451
2. Forward and Aft Rail Removal
(Figure 401)
A. References
Reference Title
52-61-00-860-801 Forward Airstair Extension (P/B 201)
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left
C. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 52-61-62-020-001
(1) Do this task: Forward Airstair Extension, TASK 52-61-00-860-801 to get access to the rail
assembly.
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 52-61-62-010-001
(1) Open the airstair door to get access to the forward rail [1] and aft rail [2].
SUBTASK 52-61-62-020-002
(2) Remove the wire harness.
(a) Disconnect the airstair electrical connector (P1) [15].
(b) Remove the speed-up limit switch, S13 [16] from the forward rail [1].
(c) Remove screws attaching the wire harness to the forward rail [1].
(d) Remove the channel [17] between the forward rail [1] and the aft rail [2].
(e) Attach the loose wire bundle and the channel [17] to the aft rail [2].
SUBTASK 52-61-62-020-003
(3) Remove the forward and aft rail bonding jumpers [3].
(a) Remove the bolts [4], washers [5], and nuts [6] from the bonding jumpers [3] on the
forward rail [1] and aft rail [2].
(b) Keep the bonding jumpers [3] attached to the floor structure. Move the wires out of the
way.
SUBTASK 52-61-62-020-004
(4) Remove the sway braces [7] that are between the first and second rail attach fittings [14] from
the floor structure.
(a) Remove the bolts [8], washers [9], and nuts [10] from the airstair brackets.
SUBTASK 52-61-62-020-005
(5) Remove the forward rail [1] from the floor structure.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Remove the shoulder bolts [11], washers [12], and nuts [13] from the rail attach
fittings [14].
(b) Remove the forward rail [1] from the airstair opening.
SUBTASK 52-61-62-020-006
(6) Remove the aft rail [2] from the floor structure.
(a) Make sure that the swing arm assembly [18] is tied to the aft rail [2].
(b) Remove the shoulder bolts [11], washers [12], and nuts [13] from the rail attach
fittings [14].
(c) Remove the aft rail [2] from the airstair opening.
52-61-62-400-801Forward and Aft Rail InstallationPDF p. 1452
3. Forward and Aft Rail Installation
(Figure 401)
A. Tools/Equipment
NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.
Reference Description
SPL-3937 Pin - Alignment, Bolt Installation
Part #: ST9501B Supplier: 81205
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 52-61-62-420-001
(1) Install the forward rail [1] and the aft rail [2] to the airplane floor structure inside the airstair door
opening.
(a) Install the alignment pins [19], (bolt installation alignment pin, SPL-3937) on the shoulder
bolts [11].
(b) Install the shoulder bolts [11] through the rail attach fittings [14].
(c) Remove the alignment pins [19], (bolt installation alignment pin, SPL-3937) and install the
washers [12] and nuts [13].
(d) Tighten the nuts between 100 in-lb (11.298 N·m) to 150 in-lb (16.948 N·m)..
SUBTASK 52-61-62-420-002
(2) Install the sway braces [7] to the airstair brackets that are between the first and second rail
attach fittings [14].
(a) Install the bolts [8], washers [9], and nuts [10] at two locations.
SUBTASK 52-61-62-420-003
(3) Do a check of the spacing between the forward rail [1] and the aft rail [2].
(a) Measure the spacing between the forward rail [1] and the aft rail [2] at the first, third, and
fifth attach fittings [14].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) If the measured dimension is more than the limits, the floor installation rail attach points
must be rechecked.
SUBTASK 52-61-62-420-004
(4) Install the bonding jumpers [3] between the floor structure, forward rail [1] and the aft rail [2].
(a) Install the bonding jumpers [3] adjacent to the outboard rail attach fittings [14].
(b) Install the bolt [4], two washers [5], and the nut [6] through the bonding jumper [3] lug into
the forward rail [1] or the aft rail [2].
(c) Install the bolt [4], three washers [5], and the nut [6] through the bonding jumper [3] lug
into the floor structure, if removed.
SUBTASK 52-61-62-420-005
(5) Install the wire harness.
(a) Install the channel [17] to the forward rail [1] and aft rail [2].
(b) Attach the wire bundle to the forward rail [1].
(c) Install the speed-up limit switch, S13 [16] to the forward rail [1].
(d) Connect the airstair electrical connector (P1) [15].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE CONDUIT SWING ARM BETWEEN THE
AIRSTAIR CARRIAGE AND THE LADDER IS IN ITS CORRECT POSITION.
IF IT IS INCORRECTLY ALIGNED , IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(e) Make sure that the swing arm conduit is correctly aligned.

F. Removal of the Entry and Galley Service Door Indication
SUBTASK 52-71-11-020-001
(1) Remove the sensor assembly [1]:
(a) For the forward entry door, do these steps:
1) Remove the bolts [23] that attach the cover [6] to the sensor assembly [1].
2) Remove the bolts [3] and washers [2] that attach the sensor assembly [1] to the
latch receiver [7].
3) For airplanes with sensor assembly P/N 284A1322-1, remove the screws [12],
washers [13], and nuts [14] that attach the proximity sensor [11] to the sensor
assembly [1].
4) For airplanes with sensor assembly P/N 284A1322-2, -3, -4, -5, -6, -7, -8, or -9,
remove the screws [12], spacers [24], and nuts [14] that attach the proximity
sensor [11] to the sensor assembly [1].
5) Cut the wires that connect the proximity sensor [11] to the airplane wiring as near as
possible to the proximity sensor [11].
6) Remove the proximity sensor [11].
(b) For the aft entry door and aft galley service door, do these steps:
1) Remove the screws [4] and washers [5] that attach the cover [6] to the sensor
assembly [1].
2) Remove the bolts [3] and washers [2] that attach the sensor assembly [1] to the
latch receiver [7].
3) Remove the screw [8], shim [26], and shims [27] that attach the sensor assembly [1]
to the fuselage frame.
4) Remove the screws [12], washers [13], and nuts [14] that attach the proximity
sensor [11] to the sensor assembly [1].
5) Cut the wires that connect the proximity sensor [11] to the airplane wiring as near as
possible to the proximity sensor [11].
6) Remove the proximity sensor [11].
(c) For the forward galley service door, do these steps:
1) Remove the screws [4] and washers [5] that attach the cover [6] to the sensor
assembly [1].
2) Remove the bolts [3] and washers [2] that attach the sensor assembly [1] to the
latch receiver [7].
3) Remove the screw [44], washer [45], shim [46], filler [47], washer [48], and nut [49]
that attach the sensor assembly [1] to the fuselage frame.
4) Remove the screws [12], washers [13], and nuts [14] that attach the proximity
sensor [11] to the sensor assembly [1].
5) Cut the wires that connect the proximity sensor [11] to the airplane wiring as near as
possible to the proximity sensor [11].
6) Remove the proximity sensor [11].

G. Adjustment of the Entry and Galley Service Door Indication Sensor
SUBTASK 52-71-11-820-005
(1) To adjust the sensor, do these steps:
(a) Get access to the PSEU through this panel:
Number Name/Location
112A Forward Access Door
(b) Use the Proximity Sensor Electronics Unit (PSEU) Built-In-Test Equipment (BITE) to test
the sensor.
1) Push the ON/OFF switch on the PSEU BITE display.
2) Push the down arrow until OTHER FUNCTNS? shows.
3) Push the YES switch to select OTHER FUNCTNS?
4) Push the down arrow until SENSOR RIGGING? shows.
5) Push the YES switch to select SENSOR RIGGING?
6) Push the down arrow until the applicable sensor identification shows.
a) Make sure that the correct code is displayed for the applicable door:
• S199 is FWD ENTR LKD
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
• S194 is FWD SERV LKD
• S200 is AFT ENTR LKD
• S195 is AFT SERV LKD
7) Push the YES switch to select the sensor.
8) Push the YES switch to select GAP GRAPH? The sensor number and clearance
display meter will show (Figure 203).
NOTE: You can also display the clearance value in MILS (1 MIL equals 1/1000th of
an inch) or required changes to the sensor clearance. Push on the down
arrow or NO switch to show these options.
(c) Make sure that the PSEU display shows the sensor clearance (blinking icon) between the
solid posts.
NOTE: If the sensor clearance is too large for detection the display will show “TGT FAR”.
(d) If the sensor clearance is not between the solid posts or TGT FAR is shown, do these
steps to adjust the sensor/target clearance:
NOTE: Get the sensor clearance as close as possible to the optimum gap clearance by
pushing the plunger flush with the surface of the latch receiver when adjusting.
The clearance can be different after the PSEU Sensor Rigging test is completed.
1) Determine what adjustment is needed for the correct sensor clearance.
a) At the GAP VALUE display, push the down arrow for the Gap Move Value.
b) Record the Gap Move Value.
NOTE: The Gap Move Value represents the distance in mils the target needs
to move toward or away from the sensor face to achieve the optimum
gap for that sensor.
2) Open the applicable door.
3) If the cover [6] is installed on the sensor assembly [1], remove the cover [6]:
a) Remove the bolts [23] or the screws [4] and washers [5] that attach the
cover [6] to the sensor assembly [1].
b) Remove the cover [6] from the sensor assembly [1].
4) If the sensor clearance is out of tolerance, do these steps:
a) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the jam nuts [15].
b) Loosen the jam nuts [15].
c) Use the recorded Gap Move Value to adjust the target position.
<1> For the Type 1 sensor assembly [1] (with one jam nut):
<a> Turn the slotted end of the plunger [10] to move the target until
the clearance is the optimum gap (Table 201).
NOTE: The clearance is applicable to the full face of the
proximity sensor.
<2> For the Type 2 sensor assembly [1] (with two jam nuts):
<a> Turn the two jam nuts [15] on the plunger [10] to move the target
until the clearance is the optimum gap (Table 201).
<3> Make sure that the target is parallel to the proximity sensor [11].
<4> If necessary adjust the target so that it is parallel to the proximity
sensor [11].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
d) Tighten the jam nuts [15].
e) Close and lock the door.
f) Examine the clearance value on the PSEU.
g) Repeat the steps to adjust the target and then check the clearance until it is
within tolerance of the optimum gap (Table 201).
Table 201/52-71-11-993-801
Sensor # Door Optimum Gap Tolerance
S199 Fwd Entry 0.1 in. (100.0 mils) +/- 0.02 in. (20.0 mils)
S200 Aft Entry 0.1 in. (100.0 mils) +/- 0.02 in. (20.0 mils)
S194 Fwd Service 0.16 in. (160.0 mils) +0.02 in. (20.0 mils) / - 0.07 in.
(70.0 mils)
S195 Aft Service 0.1 in. (100.0 mils) +/- 0.02 in. (20.0 mils)
h) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, or safety cable kit, G51827
(optional), on the jam nuts [15] (PAGEBLOCK 20-10-44/401).
(e) Do this task: Entry and Galley Service Door Indication Sensor Test (S194, S195, S199, or
S200), TASK 52-71-11-710-801.

(a) If the indication switch [22] does not actuate, do the steps that follow to adjust the

1) Measure the distance between the end of the indication switch [22] plunger and the

a) Use a 0.50 in. (12.70 mm) block of clay on the outboard face of the actuator
bracket [17].
b) Open and close the door to compress the clay.
c) Measure the clay that is left between the compression caused by the
indication switch [22] plunger and bracket [17].
2) To identify the number of shim [16] necessary for adjustment add 0.10 in. (2.54 mm)
to the measurement. This is the distance the switch plunger must be pushed.
NOTE: The total distance is the necessary shim thickness, with a tolerance of +/-
0.010 inch.
3) Prepare the number of shim [16] necessary for adjustment.
NOTE: You can use a maximum of four shims.
NOTE: Each shim has 0.032 in. (0.813 mm) solid thickness plus ten peelable shims
of 0.003 in. (0.076 mm) each, for 0.062 in. (1.575 mm) total thickness. 1
Shim - for adjustment to 0.062 in. (1.575 mm), 2 Shims - for adjustment
0.062 in. (1.575 mm) - 0.124 in. (3.150 mm), 3 Shims - for adjustment
0.124 in. (3.150 mm) - 0.186 in. (4.724 mm) and 4 Shims - for adjustment
0.186 in. (4.724 mm) - 0.248 in. (6.299 mm).
4) Drill 0.140 in. (3.56 mm) screw holes and 0.270 in. (6.86 mm), 100 degree
countersunk through shim and bracket (preferred) or drill out the rivets [25] and
discard them (alternate).
NOTE: If the shim [16] was attached with the screws [18], washers [19] and
nuts [20] to the bracket [17], then the alternate method is not applicable.
a) Align to existing hole in bracket.
5) Install the shim [16] with the solid part touching the switch plunger.
6) Install the screws [18], washers [19] and nuts [20] (preferred) or new rivets [25]
(alternate) to attach the shims [16] to the actuator bracket [17].
7) Apply Bonderite M-CR 1200S Aero coating, C50005, to bare aluminum surfaces.
8) Apply primer, C00259, to surfaces with conversion coating, including exposed
laminations of the peelable shim, after shim thickness adjustment.
9) Apply coating, C50069, on visible surfaces.

 ALL

10. Forward Entry Door Switch Test (S1147)
(Figure 205)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) This procedure is applicable for the S1147 indication switch on the forward entry door.
(2) Two mechanics can be necessary to complete this procedure. One mechanic to manually
operate the switches and the second mechanic to operate the lights in the flight compartment.
(3) For the indication sensors (S194, S195, S199, or S200) on the entry or galley service doors,
refer to Entry and Galley Service Door Indication Sensor Test (S194, S195, S199, or S200),
TASK 52-71-11-710-801.
B. References
Reference Title
52-11-00-860-803 Open the Door with the Interior Handle (P/B 201)
C. Prepare for the Procedure
SUBTASK 52-71-11-840-002
(1) Prepare for the test:
(a) Make sure that all of the doors that show on the Door Warning Panel (P5) are closed and
latched.
SUBTASK 52-71-11-720-002
(2) The system test:
(a) Push the MASTER CAUTION light on the Glareshield (P7).
1) Make sure that the MASTER CAUTION light and the DOORS light go OFF.
(b) Open the Main Entry Door.
NOTE: If it is necessary, Open the Door with the Interior Handle,
TASK 52-11-00-860-803.
1) Make sure that the MASTER CAUTION light and DOORS light on the P7 panel
come ON.
2) Make sure that the FWD ENTRY light on the P5 panel comes ON.
(c) Use your finger to push and hold the plunger on switch S1147 and switch S199.
NOTE: You will find S1147 on the aft latch receiver.
NOTE: You will find S199 on the forward latch receiver.
(d) Make sure that the FWD ENTRY light on the P5 panel goes OFF.
(e) While you hold S1147 and S199, push and release the MASTER CAUTION light on the
P7 panel.
1) Make sure that the MASTER CAUTION light and DOORS light on the P7 panel go
OFF.
(f) Release the S1147 switch.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 056-063, 067-078, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209,
212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999;  006, 007, 013, 014,

1) Make sure that the MASTER CAUTION light and DOORS light on the P7 panel
come ON.
2) Make sure that the FWD ENTRY light on the P5 panel comes ON.
(g) Close and latch the forward entry door.
1) Make sure that the FWD ENTRY light on the P5 panel goes OFF.
2) Push and release the MASTER CAUTION light on the P7 panel.
a) Make sure that the MASTER CAUTION light and DOORS light on the P7
panel go OFF.
(h) If the test is not in the limits then do these steps:
1) Make sure that the indication switch [22] is in the limits of the adjustment procedure.
a) Adjust the switch to the specified dimensions (TASK 52-71-11-820-802).
b) Close the door.
c) If the forward entry light does not go off when the door is latched and closed,
then adjust the target bracket with shims (TASK 52-71-11-820-802).
NOTE: You will find the bracket that actuates the switch on the frame of the
door.
d) If the forward entry light goes off when the door is not latched and closed,
make sure that the switch is adjusted to the specified dimensions
(TASK 52-71-11-820-802).

D. Cargo Door Indication Switch Adjustment
SUBTASK 52-71-31-820-003
(1) Make sure that the extension of the forward indication switch [1] and aft indication switch [1]
through the latch receiver [10] is 0.825 ±0.025 in. (20.96 ±0.64 mm).
NOTE: It is recommended to set the extension dimension to the high side of the tolerance if
possible. This can decrease nuisance indications caused by aircraft movement.
SUBTASK 52-71-31-820-002
(2) If necessary, adjust the forward indication switch [1] or aft indication switch [1] as follows:
(a) Put a screwdriver in the slot of the forward indication switch [1] or aft indication switch [1].
(b) Turn until the extension is correct.
SUBTASK 52-71-31-410-001
(3) If the cargo door is open, close it.
(a) Remove the strap from the lower stop.

(1) Do a test of the forward indication switch [1] or aft indication switch [1] as follows:

(e) Close the applicable cargo door.
(f) Make sure that the FWD CARGO or AFT CARGO light goes off.
